title: A Day in Athens
subtitle: On murals, on pottery, in life.

items.text: Theater Plaza
Lively songs float across the open ground, while wine jugs and sacrifices are raised, weaving their way through the colorful crowd.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: A scene only recorded in ancient tomes and murals now comes alive before my eyes ...

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: Merely on the merits of historical research alone, the invention of Huygens-Fresnel Interferometer is truly miraculous!

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Looks like X will have a permanent guinea pig for this experiment of his.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: Most certainly.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Just don't forget to bring us along, eh?

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Because after this, I'm not letting you leave my sight. No matter if you head to a robotics lab or the dark side of the moon!
As they cheer and laugh, Perikles ascends the central stage and begins a speech.

items.speaker: Perikles
items.text: Fellow Athenians and distinguished friends from every polis—

items.speaker: Perikles
items.text: It is with great joy that we gathered here to mark the beginning of the Dionysia.

items.speaker: Perikles
items.text: Tragedy—is an eternal art form that speaks an enduring truth, and just as it endures, so too shall our civilization.

items.speaker: Perikles
items.text: Let no man, no foe, strip us of the right to bask in its timeless beauty.

items.speaker: Perikles
items.text: We do not bow to fear or menace, nor to any enemy, be they known or unknown.
Below the stage, Kassandra wraps up the scytale and stores it away.

items.speaker: Kassandra
items.text: When the Great Dionysos arrives, the Owl of Athena will whisper,

items.speaker: Kassandra
items.text: as Deimos descends into the mortal world.

items.speaker: Kassandra
items.text: Could Alexios ... No, Deimos, really stand such a provocation?
The Spear of Leonidas is gripped in her hand as Ikaros soars above the venue.
Kassandra's search doesn't take long. Her target presents himself just beyond the plaza's entrance.

items.speaker: Alexios
items.text: Perikles. Soon enough the cult will claim you.

items.speaker: Alexios
items.text: A necessary sacrifice to unify the Greeks.

items.speaker: Evzone
items.text: Protect Perikles!!

items.speaker: Kassandra
items.text: I cannot believe what has become of you ...

items.speaker: Alexios
items.text: You've arrived much faster than I thought, misthios.

items.speaker: Alexios
items.text: I should have known better than to trust in that secret code.
He raises the Sword of Damokles high. Its cold, sharp reflection casting halos in the sunlight.

items.speaker: Alexios
items.text: Do not get in my way! I will deal with you once I have Perikles's head.

items.speaker: Cultist I
items.text: Deimos, leave the misthios to us. Perikles must be slain!
Black-clad warriors rush out from the crowd; they cast off their robes to reveal dark armor that glints under the sun.

items.speaker: Kassandra
items.text: You will not run from me again.
Kassandra lifts her spear, her body tensing as she readies for the fight to come.

items.speaker: Kassandra
items.text: Our war ends today.

items.speaker: Evzone
items.text: You are not alone, Misthios.
Battle cries erupt from all across the festival grounds.

items.speaker: Cultist II
items.text: Malaka! Our plan has been discovered! Domitius betrayed us!
The cultist curses as the Evzoni form up their lines.

items.speaker: Cultist II
items.text: There is no end to the punishment that awaits him!

items.speaker: Cultist I
items.text: Calm down, Orestēs! Have faith in the Sage's plans. These brutes stand no chance against our numbers!

items.speaker: Cultist I
items.text: Kill them all!
The panicked, scattering crowd only adds to the chaos of the situation.
Made worse by the growing number of cultists that join the fray, keeping the Evzoni divided.

items.speaker: Evzone
items.text: Kassandra! These cultists are hiding among the civilians; we cannot hope to keep the Strategos safe here.

items.speaker: Evzone
items.text: Get Perikles to safety!

items.speaker: Perikles
items.text: Protect yourselves first.

items.speaker: Perikles
items.text: You've done all that you could to prevent this, Kassandra. It was my hubris that led us to hold the Dionysia. I must accept my fate.
Alexios ascends the stage confidently casting aside the remaining Evzoni. His sword humming in his hand.

items.speaker: Alexios
items.text: Fate, indeed. Your fate is already foretold, old man. We have arranged each and every moment.

items.speaker: Alexios
items.text: Do you think knowing our plan would be enough to stop it?

items.speaker: Alexios
items.text: Look at the death you have brought on your own people ...
The chaos of the fighting has grown into a wild pandemonium.

items.speaker: Athenian I
items.text: SAVE YOURSELVES! RUN!!!

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: What's all the fuss?

items.speaker: Athenian II
items.text: Get out of my way, foreigner! I'm not going to die in this place!
Panicked festival goers are rushing around the plaza in every direction, complicating the battle even further.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: Hold on, madam, you're headed the wrong way!

items.speaker: Athenian III
items.text: I'm not leaving! If we let the Dionysia end this way, it will surely bring his wrath down on Athens!

items.speaker: Athenian III
items.text: I fear the gods more than I fear the blades of men!

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Regulus, Mr. APPLe, we need to help Kassandra.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: What's your plan then? Because I don't see a way to get through that bloody mosh pit!

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Not that I've ever been to a gig with this many swords.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Maybe not, but there might be some value in looking at this in the same way as one might manage a rowdy music festival.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Even the wildest crowd can be swayed by the right performance.
She scans the chaotic scene; spying dramatic masks, wreaths of grapevines and ivy, golden statues of gods and heroes, and altars laden with offerings.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: The problem is, what would get their attention? A story maybe ... one of Dionysos's legends, or maybe a crowd-pleasing epic ...

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: Vertin, if you're in need of some historical suggestions, this APPLe is ready to assist.
His offer of support rings like a melody in her ears. But it's his appearance that gives her an idea.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Yes, Mr. APPLe, I do believe YOU are exactly what I need.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: Wait, now hold on! Will either of you tell me why you've decided to gild me ... again!?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I'll ask you to stop wriggling, Mr. APPLe. This paint is all we've got left from making our masks.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Fab! Oh, but you missed a spot, a little more gold over here, please!
